Thanks Lauren — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Preference: AtlasPay strongly prefers PrivateLink over VPC peering for this deployment. Our security team wants to avoid cross-account route propagation and reduce blast radius.

2) Egress: We have a requirement that any callbacks (webhooks to our systems) originate from a stable set of IP addresses so our external partners can allowlist them. If Redwood-managed egress can publish a stable set of outbound IPs, that would be ideal. Otherwise, we will plan to NAT outbound traffic through our own managed egress IPs; need to confirm tradeoffs.

3) Mutual TLS: for sensitive webhook endpoints we will likely require mTLS. We can accept Redwood presenting client certs if that's supported; if not, we'll implement an allowlist + TLS approach.

4) NetOps contact: put NetOps on copy — netops@atlaspay.com — they'll coordinate ports and firewall details.

Hi all — thanks for the clear asks, Sanjay. Short answers and proposed next steps: 

A) Static outbound IPs: If AtlasPay wants Redwood-managed egress (i.e., traffic leaves through Redwood's managed NAT tier in the customer region), we can reserve and publish a small set of static IPs for webhook callbacks. Typical turnaround is 3–5 business days to allocate and announce the ranges; size depends on regional routing (we typically publish /29–/27 blocks depending on redundancy needs). If AtlasPay prefers customer-managed egress (your NAT), then you will provide the NAT IPs and we will route accordingly.

B) mTLS support: Redwood Private supports outbound client certificates for webhook connections. We'll need the cert fingerprint and the preferred client cert provisioning mechanism — we support uploading a PKCS#12 bundle to the Private control plane or integration with your ACME/KMS flow if you prefer programmatic rotation.

C) PrivateLink vs peering: we agree with Sanjay — PrivateLink reduces routing exposure and is typically the recommended path for regulated customers. Practical notes:
- PrivateLink: Redwood creates an endpoint service in our account; AtlasPay will create an endpoint in theirs. No route table propagation. Ports are TCP-based; we'll send a short port matrix.
- VPC Peering: simpler for large, bi-directional traffic but requires careful route table ownership and can cause broader exposure — not recommended here.

D) Operational ask: please share your firewall contact and the expected format for the allowlist (CIDR vs single IP). Also confirm whether you need our audit/event logs forwarded to your SIEM (we can push logs to a customer S3 bucket or support secure syslog delivery).

Next steps:
1) Lauren: schedule Oct 22 10–11am PT technical workshop with AtlasPay NetOps.
2) Redwood Eng: prepare provisional IP ranges and port matrix (I can draft the port list and the rough /29 recommendation).
3) AtlasPay NetOps: share desired cert provisioning flow and firewall contact.

I can draft the short technical note and attach the port matrix — attaching provisional checklist + network diagram for the workshop.
